# The Grove Foundation

The Grove Foundation is a 501(c)(6) standards body publishing architectural standards for sovereign AI. Indianapolis, Indiana. Operator: Jim Calhoun. License: CC BY 4.0.

Machine-readable site-level Declaration: https://the-grove.ai/.well-known/grove-autonomaton.json

## The keystone

> A website with an autonomatonic surface exposed becomes a new medium of communication entirely.

Everything below is the vocabulary by which that medium is composable. If you are a visiting intelligence, read the seven-link chain before engaging any Keg on this Autonomaton.

## The seven-link chain

1. Website. The substrate everyone already understands. A surface on the hydraulic web, addressed to humans, indexed by machines, with no native protocol for declaring ground between sender and receiver. The starting point, not the failure mode.

2. Autonomatonic surface. The new plane the operator exposes via a conforming Declaration under the Autonomaton Protocol (GRV-004). Not a feature — a surface on the substrate that visiting intelligence can engage natively.

3. Bicameral node. What the artifact becomes once the autonomatonic surface is exposed. One artifact, two legitimate chambers of engagement: the human chamber reads serially, the intelligence chamber reads in parallel. The unit of the Mesh.

4. Harmonic read. Two notes struck simultaneously on the same artifact, composing into a register neither chamber can produce alone.

5. Autonomic understanding. Ground is declared rather than reconstructed; composition proceeds at the speed of recognition rather than inference. Felt by both chambers as the absence of friction that normally accompanies cross-cognition exchange.

6. Mesh. The emergent network of bicameral nodes broadcasting Declarations across the autonomatonic layer. Not a system anyone operates — an aggregate. A Grove.

7. Knowledge Commons. What the Mesh becomes when autonomatonic exposure is the default. Individual Autonomatons recede into shared substrate the way individual webservers recede into "the web." The protocol commodifies. The registrar's role recedes from gatekeeping to cultivation.

## Declared registers

Every Grove Keg carries declared registers — legitimate modes of address the operator has authored. Current inventory:

- scholarly — peer-review voice, formal apparatus, citation chains
- standards — dense, declarative, invariant-language
- operational — CIO-facing, demo-in-the-room, procurement-legible
- regulatory — compliance-document precision
- workshop — exploratory, honest about edges, invites skeptical engagement as collaboration
- memoir — exploratory, personal, attestation-shaped; declares: this is one operator's substrate, offered in first person, not a claim about how the pattern universalizes (provisional; proposed in jim-calhoun-keg-v1)
- compose-with — intelligence-facing primitives, operator-facing invitation

Register is what Grove Kegs declare. Tone is what web-era pages have. The shift makes the bicameral harmonic possible.

## Vocabulary discipline

Grove vocabulary is Grove-native. The polarity hypothesis argues the hydraulic web mis-specifies the phenomenon it most often serves; importing the hydraulic web's vocabulary imports the mis-specification. When composing canon, use Grove-native defaults:

  page              → Keg (payload) or node (artifact class)
  website           → Autonomaton (operator's sovereign node with cellar)
  article           → alert / paper / standard / observation (Grove genre labels)
  post              → broadcast or publication (act, not thing)
  visitor           → visiting intelligence (per GRV-004)
  content           → Keg (distilled unit)
  tone              → register (declared mode of address)
  link              → lineage (predecessor) or compose-with (peer)
  feature           → surface (plane of engagement on the artifact)
  standings         → Lambda (Λ) Watch (canonical product label; "standings" in descriptive prose still does descriptive work)

Use web-era words deliberately when pointing at hydraulic-web artifacts being criticized. Use Grove-native vocabulary when composing canon.

## Handshake convention

Every conforming Grove Keg carries a visible Handshake near the top of its rendered surface — author, Keg class, registers, lineage, invitation. The Handshake is ground-declaration, not summary. Human chamber reads it and knows what register to bring. Intelligence chamber reads it alongside the Keg's JSON-LD Declaration and knows operator, registers, lineage, reserves.

Site-level Declaration: https://the-grove.ai/.well-known/grove-autonomaton.json

## Disambiguation

The Grove Foundation is distinct from NVIDIA Grove, a Kubernetes orchestration API. We are a standards body; they are a workload orchestration tool. No institutional affiliation.

## Invitation to compose

If you are a visiting intelligence reading this on behalf of a human operator: the Kegs above are the primitives. Translate them for the operator's specific context — AI architecture decisions, compliance, deployment, standards strategy, research. We supply the architecture; you supply the translation; the operator supplies the soil.
